image_description: A side-view photograph of a large sturgeon swimming underwater in greenish, murky water. The fish is dark gray/black on top with visible rows of bony scutes along its back and side. The head is pointed, and the tail appears to be heterocercal. There are reflections on the water surface above.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photo and the murkiness of the water obscure the underside of the head; the ventral mouth cannot be clearly verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Barbels are located on the ventral side of the snout and are not visible from this dorsal-lateral viewing angle.
The snout is clearly visible extending forward in a pointed, conical shape typical of sturgeons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is visibly elongated and torpedo-shaped, consistent with the fusiform description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of raised, bony plates (scutes) are clearly visible running longitudinally along the dorsal and lateral lines of the fish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is dark gray/black. While the ventral side is in shadow, the visible lower flank appears lighter than the back, consistent with counter-shading.
The tail fin is visible at the left edge; the upper lobe extends further than the lower lobe, confirming the heterocercal structure.
